gloss: be right, righteous; righteousness; righteous; justify
summary: The root is being right: in the right before a judge, right by the standard (a just weight, a just measure), and right in conduct toward God and man. צֶדֶק and צְדָקָה are the rightness itself, done (“to do righteousness and justice”), spoken, judged and ruled by; צַדִּיק is the man who is in the right and does right, set again and again against the רָשָׁע, the wicked; the verb is to be in the right, and in the hiphil to declare or make another so, to justify. Yahweh is righteous, and his righteousness is what he does to keep his word and save his people, so that “my righteousness” stands beside “my salvation”. Scripture reckons righteousness to Abraham's faith (Gen 15:6), promises a righteous branch of David who will reign and do righteousness in the land, named “Yahweh our righteousness” (Jer 23:5–6), and a righteous servant who will justify many and bear their iniquities (Isa 53:11).

words.gloss: righteous, just; in the right; the righteous (man)
words.summary: About 206 times, most in Psalms, Proverbs and Ezekiel, and most often as a noun, “the righteous (one)”. Its constant opposite is רָשָׁע “wicked”: the two are judged apart, and to treat them alike is what the Judge of all the earth will not do (Gen 18:25).

senses.gloss: righteous (of a man): doing right before God
senses.definition: A man who does what is right by God's standard: who walks in his statutes, keeps his judgments, does justice and righteousness, and does not oppress. Set against the wicked, the sinner and the man of injustice.

evidence.note: “Noah was a man צַדִּיק, תָּמִים in his generations; Noah walked with God.”
“You I have seen צַדִּיק before me in this generation.”
“If a man is צַדִּיק and does justice and righteousness …” then the deeds listed, ending: “in my statutes he walks and my judgments he keeps, to do truth: צַדִּיק הוּא, living he will live.”
“Yahweh knows the way of צַדִּיקִים, but the way of רְשָׁעִים will perish.”
“You will see between צַדִּיק and רָשָׁע, between one serving God and one who does not serve him.”
“An abomination to צַדִּיקִים is a man of injustice, and an abomination to the wicked is one upright of way.”
“צַדִּיקִים will inherit the land and dwell forever upon it.”
“The memory of צַדִּיק is for a blessing, but the name of the wicked will rot.”
“There is not a man צַדִּיק on the earth who does good and does not sin.”
“וְצַדִּיק בֶּאֱמוּנָתוֹ יִחְיֶה”: the righteous will live by his faithfulness.

senses.gloss: in the right (in a dispute or case); innocent
senses.definition: In a cause between two, the one who is right and not guilty. A judge is to declare him so, and not the wicked.

evidence.note: When men have a dispute, the judges “וְהִצְדִּיקוּ אֶת הַצַּדִּיק וְהִרְשִׁיעוּ אֶת הָרָשָׁע”.
“וְנָקִי וְצַדִּיק do not kill, for I will not justify the wicked”: צַדִּיק beside נָקִי “innocent”.
Saul to David: “צַדִּיק אַתָּה מִמֶּנִּי, for you did me good and I did you evil.”
Pharaoh: “I have sinned this time; יַהְוֶה הַצַּדִּיק, and I and my people הָרְשָׁעִים.”
Jehu to the people: “צַדִּקִים אַתֶּם”: you are not guilty; I conspired.
“One who justifies the wicked and one who condemns צַדִּיק, both are an abomination to Yahweh.”
“Oppressors of צַדִּיק, takers of a bribe.”

senses.gloss: righteous (of Yahweh, his judgments and laws)
senses.definition: Yahweh is righteous: he does no wrong, judges rightly, and keeps his word; so are his judgments and his law. Israel confesses it when his judgment falls on them.

evidence.note: “A God of faithfulness and without injustice, צַדִּיק וְיָשָׁר הוּא.”
“There is no other God besides me, אֵל צַדִּיק וּמוֹשִׁיעַ; there is none but me.”
“יַהְוֶה צַדִּיק in her midst; he does not do injustice.”
“God is שׁוֹפֵט צַדִּיק.”
“For יַהְוֶה צַדִּיק; he loves righteousness.”
“צַדִּיק יַהְוֶה in all his ways.”
“You have established your words, for צַדִּיק אָתָּה”: righteous in keeping his promise to Abraham.
“You are צַדִּיק concerning all that has come upon us, for you have done truth, and we have done wickedly.”
“For צַדִּיק is Yahweh our God in all his works which he has done, and we have not listened to his voice.”
“צַדִּיק הוּא יַהְוֶה, for I have rebelled against his mouth.”
“Statutes and judgments צַדִּיקִם as all this law.”
“צַדִּיק אַתָּה יַהְוֶה, and upright are your judgments.”

senses.gloss: the righteous one: the promised king and servant
senses.definition: The ruler, king, branch and servant whom Yahweh promises are called צַדִּיק: the one who rules over men righteous, the righteous branch of David, the king who comes to Zion, and the righteous servant who justifies many. The New Testament calls Jesus “the Righteous One”.

evidence.note: David's last words: “מוֹשֵׁל בָּאָדָם צַדִּיק, ruling in the fear of God.”
“I will raise up to David צֶמַח צַדִּיק, and he shall reign as king … and do justice and righteousness in the land.”
“Behold, your king comes to you, צַדִּיק וְנוֹשָׁע הוּא, humble and riding on a donkey.”
“By his knowledge יַצְדִּיק צַדִּיק עַבְדִּי לָרַבִּים, and he will bear their iniquities.”
“You denied the holy and righteous one (δίκαιον).”
The prophets “announced beforehand the coming of the righteous one (τοῦ δικαίου)”.
Paul chosen “to see the righteous one (τὸν δίκαιον)”.
“Christ suffered once for sins, righteous for unrighteous (δίκαιος ὑπὲρ ἀδίκων).”

evidence.locator: Hab.2.4, צַדִּיק → δίκαιος; Exo.23.7 → δίκαιον; Psa.34.16 → δικαίους; Pro.11.31 → δίκαιος; δίκαιος renders צַדִּיק ×182

evidence.note: Hab 2:4 quoted: “ὁ δὲ δίκαιος ἐκ πίστεως ζήσεται”; also Gal 3:11; Heb 10:38.
Psa 34:16 quoted: “the eyes of the Lord are on the righteous (ἐπὶ δικαίους)”.
Pro 11:31 in the Greek: “if the righteous (ὁ δίκαιος) is scarcely saved …”.

opposites.note: “Wicked”, guilty: the commonest pairing of the word, in law, psalm and proverb.

evidence.note: “Will you sweep away צַדִּיק עִם רָשָׁע?”
“The righteousness of הַצַּדִּיק will be upon him, and the wickedness of הָרָשָׁע will be upon him.”
“The wicked surrounds הַצַּדִּיק; therefore justice goes forth perverted.”
“Sinners in the congregation of צַדִּיקִים.”
“Rejoice, צַדִּיקִים, and shout for joy, all upright of heart.”

words.summary: About 155 times. More than צֶדֶק it is righteousness done: a man's deeds, the king's rule, Yahweh's acts of deliverance (plural צִדְקוֹת), and the righteousness reckoned to Abraham.

senses.definition: What a man does that is right by God's commandments; with עָשָׂה and מִשְׁפָּט, “to do justice and righteousness”. A man's righteousness can be turned from, and then is not remembered.

evidence.note: Abraham will command his children “to keep the way of Yahweh לַעֲשׂוֹת צְדָקָה וּמִשְׁפָּט”.
If the wicked turns and “does justice וּצְדָקָה, living he will live … בְּצִדְקָתוֹ אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה he will live”.
“When the righteous turns מִצִּדְקָתוֹ and does injustice … כָּל צִדְקֹתָיו which he did will not be remembered.”
“He trusts in his righteousness and does injustice: all his righteousnesses will not be remembered.”
“Keep justice וַעֲשׂוּ צְדָקָה.”
“Do justice and righteousness, and deliver the robbed from the hand of the oppressor.”
“To do צְדָקָה and justice is chosen by Yahweh more than sacrifice.”
“In the path of צְדָקָה is life, and in its pathway no death.”
“Happy … the doer of צְדָקָה at all times.”
“He has scattered, he has given to the poor; צִדְקָתוֹ stands forever.”
“All צִדְקֹתֵינוּ are like a menstrual rag.”

senses.definition: With חָשַׁב “count, reckon” or הָיָה לְ “be to”: what God counts as righteousness to a man, Abraham's believing, Phinehas's zeal, keeping the commandment, returning a pledge.

evidence.note: “וְהֶאֱמִן בַּיַהְוֶה וַיַּחְשְׁבֶהָ לּוֹ צְדָקָה.” Quoted Rom 4:3; Gal 3:6; Jas 2:23.
Of Phinehas: “וַתֵּחָשֶׁב לוֹ לִצְדָקָה, to generation and generation, until forever.”
“וּצְדָקָה תִּהְיֶה לָּנוּ if we keep to do all this commandment before Yahweh our God.”
Return the poor man's pledge at sunset, “and to you it will be צְדָקָה before Yahweh your God”.
“ἐπίστευσεν δὲ Ἀβραὰμ τῷ θεῷ, καὶ ἐλογίσθη αὐτῷ εἰς δικαιοσύνην.”

senses.gloss: one's own righteousness (not the ground of God's gift)
senses.definition: A man's or a people's own righteousness, which scripture says is not why God gives the land or answers prayer.

evidence.note: “Do not say in your heart, בְּצִדְקָתִי Yahweh brought me in … לֹא בְצִדְקָתְךָ … for you are a stiff-necked people.”
“Not on צִדְקֹתֵינוּ do we lay our pleas before you, but on your great compassions.”
“צִדְקַת הַצַּדִּיק will not deliver him in the day of his transgression.”

senses.gloss: Yahweh's righteousness; his righteous acts of deliverance
senses.definition: What Yahweh does as the righteous God: his acts for his people (plural צִדְקוֹת), and his righteousness set beside his salvation, near, revealed, and lasting forever.

evidence.note: “There they recount צִדְקוֹת יַהְוֶה”: Deborah's song of the victory.
Samuel will plead “all צִדְקוֹת יַהְוֶה which he did with you and with your fathers”: the exodus and the judges (vv. 8–11).
“Remember … from Shittim to Gilgal, to know צִדְקוֹת יַהְוֶה.”
“I bring near צִדְקָתִי, it will not be far, and my salvation will not linger.”
“My salvation will be forever, וְצִדְקָתִי will not be broken.”
“My salvation is near to come, וְצִדְקָתִי to be revealed.”
“His arm saved for him, וְצִדְקָתוֹ upheld him; he put on צְדָקָה as a breastplate.”
“בְּצִדְקָתְךָ deliver me and rescue me.”
“Yahweh has made known his salvation; to the eyes of the nations he has revealed צִדְקָתוֹ.”
His covenant faithfulness on those who fear him, “וְצִדְקָתוֹ to children's children”.
“לְךָ אֲדֹנָי הַצְּדָקָה, and to us shame of face.”
“According to all צִדְקֹתֶךָ, let your anger turn from your city.”

senses.definition: The king's doing of justice and righteousness for his people, by which a throne stands; promised above all of David's son and branch.

evidence.note: “David was doing justice וּצְדָקָה for all his people.”
The queen of Sheba: Yahweh “set you as king to do justice and righteousness”.
“By צְדָקָה a throne is established.”
“Give your judgments to the king, וְצִדְקָתְךָ to the king's son.”
On the throne of David, “to establish it with justice וּבִצְדָקָה from now and forever”.
The righteous branch “shall do justice and righteousness in the land (בָּאָרֶץ)”.
“A branch of צְדָקָה … and he shall do justice and righteousness in the land.”
Of Josiah: “he did justice and righteousness; then it was good for him.”
“The work of הַצְּדָקָה will be peace.”

senses.definition: A right or just claim that a man has, or the honest dealing that will answer for him.

evidence.note: Mephibosheth: “What צְדָקָה do I still have, to cry still to the king?”
“To you there is no portion וּצְדָקָה and memorial in Jerusalem.”
Jacob: “צִדְקָתִי will answer for me in a day to come”: his honesty in the wages.

evidence.locator: Gen.15.6, צְדָקָה → δικαιοσύνην; Psa.106.31 → δικαιοσύνην; Gen.18.19 → δικαιοσύνην; δικαιοσύνη renders צְדָקָה ×123

evidence.note: Gen 15:6 quoted: “ἐλογίσθη αὐτῷ εἰς δικαιοσύνην”; also Rom 4:9, 22; Gal 3:6; Jas 2:23.

evidence.locator: Deu.6.25, צְדָקָה → ἐλεημοσύνη; Deu.24.13; Psa.24.5; Psa.33.5; Psa.103.6

evidence.note: “When you do ἐλεημοσύνην, do not sound a trumpet”: the Peshitta has זֵדֿקתָֿא, its word of this root (see זֵדְקְתָא).
“Your prayer is heard, and αἱ ἐλεημοσύναι σου are remembered before God.”

parallels.note: “Justice, judgment”: the fixed pair, “to do justice and righteousness”.

evidence.note: “He waited לְמִשְׁפָּט, and behold bloodshed (מִשְׂפָּח); לִצְדָקָה, and behold a cry (צְעָקָה).”
“Let justice roll down like waters, וּצְדָקָה like an ever-flowing stream.”

parallels.note: “Salvation”: Yahweh's righteousness set beside his salvation.

evidence.note: “A pursuer of צְדָקָה וָחָסֶד will find life, righteousness and honour.”
“I am Yahweh, doing חֶסֶד, justice וּצְדָקָה in the earth.”
“בְּצִדְקָתִי … וּבְרִשְׁעַת הַגּוֹיִם הָאֵלֶּה.”

words.gloss: rightness, righteousness; what is right; vindication
words.summary: About 120 times. It names the quality of being right by the standard: of a weight and measure, of a judgment, of words, of a man's way and of God's rule; and the right that is vindicated when God judges. The brief's count includes the names Melchizedek and Adoni-zedek, which are spelled with it.

senses.gloss: right, true to the standard (of weights, measures, paths, sacrifices)
senses.definition: In a construct phrase, what is right and as it should be: an honest balance and measure, right paths, sacrifices offered rightly.

evidence.note: “מֹאזְנֵי צֶדֶק אַבְנֵי צֶדֶק אֵיפַת צֶדֶק וְהִין צֶדֶק you shall have.”
“A full וָצֶדֶק stone, a full וָצֶדֶק ephah”: beside שְׁלֵמָה “whole, full”.
“Let him weigh me בְמֹאזְנֵי צֶדֶק, and God will know my integrity.”
“He leads me בְמַעְגְּלֵי צֶדֶק for his name's sake.”
“Sacrifice זִבְחֵי צֶדֶק and trust in Yahweh”; also Deu 33:19; Psa 51:21.

senses.definition: Judging rightly, without favour to small or great; the judge's duty, and Yahweh's as judge of the world.

evidence.note: “You shall not lift the face of the poor nor honour the face of the great; בְּצֶדֶק תִּשְׁפֹּט your neighbour.”
“Judge צֶדֶק between a man and his brother and his sojourner.”
Judges “shall judge the people מִשְׁפַּט צֶדֶק”.
“צֶדֶק צֶדֶק תִּרְדֹּף, that you may live and possess the land.”
“He will judge the world בְּצֶדֶק”; also Psa 96:13; 98:9.
The shoot of Jesse: “he will judge the poor בְּצֶדֶק.”
“Yahweh of armies, שֹׁפֵט צֶדֶק, testing kidneys and heart.”
“Open your mouth, judge צֶדֶק, and plead the cause of the poor and needy.”
“The place of הַצֶּדֶק, there was wickedness.”

senses.definition: What is right and true in what is said, set against lying and deceit.

evidence.note: “You love evil more than good, falsehood (שֶׁקֶר) more than speaking צֶדֶק.”
“He who breathes out faithfulness declares צֶדֶק, but a witness of falsehoods, deceit.”
“בְּצֶדֶק are all the words of my mouth; there is nothing twisted or crooked in them.”
“I am Yahweh, speaking צֶדֶק, declaring uprightness.”

senses.definition: Right conduct and character, loved, done, put on as a garment, sought and learned.

evidence.note: Who may dwell on the holy hill: “one walking blameless וּפֹעֵל צֶדֶק and speaking truth in his heart”.
“You love צֶדֶק and hate רֶשַׁע; therefore God, your God, has anointed you.” Quoted Heb 1:9.
“צֶדֶק I put on, and it clothed me.”
“Let your priests be clothed with צֶדֶק.”
The faithful city, full of justice, “צֶדֶק lodged in her, but now murderers”.
“When your judgments are in the earth, the inhabitants of the world learn צֶדֶק.”
“Listen to me, pursuers of צֶדֶק, seekers of Yahweh.”
“Seek Yahweh … seek צֶדֶק, seek humility.”
“I, בְּצֶדֶק, will see your face; I will be satisfied when I awake with your likeness.”

senses.definition: The rightness of a man's cause, which he asks God to judge and bring to light.

evidence.note: “Judge me, Yahweh, כְּצִדְקִי and according to my integrity.”
“Hear, Yahweh, צֶדֶק; attend to my cry.”
“Judge me כְצִדְקְךָ, Yahweh my God.”
“He will bring out צִדְקֶךָ like the light, and your justice like the noonday.”
“Yahweh rewarded me כְּצִדְקִי, according to the cleanness of my hands.”
“Turn back: צִדְקִי is still in it.”
“Answer me when I call, God of צִדְקִי.”

senses.gloss: God's righteousness: the ground of his throne, his saving help
senses.definition: The righteousness of Yahweh as judge and king, the foundation of his throne; and his righteousness as the help that holds up his servant and comes near as salvation.

evidence.note: “צֶדֶק וּמִשְׁפָּט are the foundation of your throne.” Also Psa 97:2.
“I will uphold you בִּימִין צִדְקִי.”
“קָרוֹב צִדְקִי, my salvation has gone out.”
“Let the skies pour down צֶדֶק; let the earth open and bring forth salvation.”
“I, Yahweh, have called you בְצֶדֶק … for a covenant of the people, for a light of the nations.”
“צֶדֶק and peace have kissed … צֶדֶק looks down from heaven.”
“צִדְקָתְךָ is צֶדֶק forever.”
“Until he comes and rains צֶדֶק upon you.”

senses.gloss: righteousness of the coming king and age
senses.definition: The righteousness in which the promised king will reign and the everlasting righteousness the seventy sevens are to bring in; the name the branch and Jerusalem will bear.

evidence.note: “Behold, לְצֶדֶק a king will reign, and princes will rule for justice.”
“צֶדֶק will be the belt of his loins.”
“This is his name by which he will be called: יַהְוֶה צִדְקֵנוּ.”
The same name given to Jerusalem: “this is what one will call her: יַהְוֶה צִדְקֵנוּ.”
“Seventy sevens are determined … to cover (וּלְכַפֵּר) iniquity וּלְהָבִיא צֶדֶק עֹלָמִים.”
“Afterward you will be called עִיר הַצֶּדֶק, a faithful city.”
“Yahweh bless you, נְוֵה צֶדֶק, mountain of holiness.”
“You are a priest forever after the order of מַלְכִּי צֶדֶק.”

evidence.locator: Psa.45.8, צֶדֶק → δικαιοσύνην; Psa.96.13 → δικαιοσύνῃ; Psa.98.9; Psa.9.9; Dan.9.24 → δικαιοσύνην; δικαιοσύνη renders צֶדֶק ×81

evidence.note: Psa 45:8 quoted of the son: “ἠγάπησας δικαιοσύνην καὶ ἐμίσησας ἀνομίαν.”
God “has set a day in which he will judge the world in righteousness (κρίνειν τὴν οἰκουμένην ἐν δικαιοσύνῃ) by a man whom he has appointed”: the words of Psa 9:9; 96:13; 98:9.
Melchizedek “interpreted, king of righteousness (βασιλεὺς δικαιοσύνης)”.

parallels.note: “Justice, judgment”: the pair of the throne and of the judge.

evidence.note: “I will betroth you to me בְּצֶדֶק וּבְמִשְׁפָּט, in covenant faithfulness and compassion.”

opposites.note: “Wickedness”: loved or hated against צֶדֶק, found in its place.

words.gloss: be in the right, be righteous; justify, declare righteous
words.summary: About 41 times. The qal is being in the right, above all in a case before a judge or before God; the hiphil is the judge's act of declaring a man in the right, and also making many righteous; the piel is showing someone righteous, the hithpael clearing oneself.

stems.gloss: be in the right; be righteous, be justified

senses.gloss: be in the right (in a case), be more righteous than
senses.definition: To have the right on one's side when two are compared or judged; with מִן, to be more in the right than another.

evidence.note: Judah of Tamar: “צָדְקָה מִמֶּנִּי, because I did not give her to Shelah my son.”
“I have set out my case; I know that I אֶצְדָּק.”
“Let us plead together; recount, that you may be in the right (לְמַעַן תִּצְדָּק).”
“Let them bring their witnesses וְיִצְדָּקוּ, and let them hear and say, Truth.”
“Will you condemn me that you may be in the right (לְמַעַן תִּצְדָּק)?”
“In this you are not right (לֹא צָדַקְתָּ).”
“That you may be in the right (תִּצְדַּק) when you speak, blameless when you judge.” Quoted Rom 3:4.

senses.gloss: be righteous (before God, by his standard)
senses.definition: To be righteous in God's sight; asked of man, and denied of every man living; said of Yahweh's judgments; promised of Israel's seed in Yahweh.

evidence.note: “Do not enter into judgment with your servant, for לֹא יִצְדַּק before you any living.” Echoed Rom 3:20; Gal 2:16.
“How can a man יִצְדַּק with God?”; also Job 25:4.
“Can a man be righteous (יִצְדָּק) before God?”
“The judgments of Yahweh are truth; צָדְקוּ altogether.”
“In Yahweh all the seed of Israel יִצְדְּקוּ and will glory.”

senses.gloss: be put right, restored to its right state
senses.definition: Of the sanctuary after its desolation: to be set right again.

evidence.note: “Until evening, morning, 2,300; then וְנִצְדַּק קֹדֶשׁ.”

senses.gloss: show to be righteous (by comparison); justify (oneself, another)
senses.definition: To make another appear righteous by being worse than he, or to clear oneself or another.

evidence.note: “צִדְּקָה נַפְשָׁהּ, apostate Israel, more than treacherous Judah.”
“You multiplied your abominations more than they, וַתְּצַדְּקִי your sisters.”
Elihu's anger against Job “because צַדְּקוֹ נַפְשׁוֹ rather than God”.
“Speak, for I desire צַדְּקֶךָּ.”

stems.gloss: declare righteous, justify; do justice; make righteous

senses.gloss: declare in the right, acquit, justify
senses.definition: The judge's act: to pronounce the one in the right to be so, the opposite of הִרְשִׁיעַ “condemn”. To justify the wicked is forbidden and abhorred.

evidence.note: “וְהִצְדִּיקוּ אֶת הַצַּדִּיק וְהִרְשִׁיעוּ אֶת הָרָשָׁע.”
“To condemn (לְהַרְשִׁיעַ) the wicked … וּלְהַצְדִּיק צַדִּיק, to give him according to his righteousness.” Also 2Ch 6:23.
Yahweh: “לֹא אַצְדִּיק רָשָׁע.”
“מַצְדִּיק רָשָׁע and one condemning the righteous: an abomination to Yahweh, both of them.”
“מַצְדִּיקֵי רָשָׁע for a bribe.”
The servant: “קָרוֹב מַצְדִּיקִי; who will contend with me?”
“Far be it from me that I should justify you (אַצְדִּיק אֶתְכֶם).”
“Who will bring a charge against God's chosen? God is the one who justifies (ὁ δικαιῶν)”: the words of Isa 50:8–9.

senses.definition: To give a man his right in a cause, especially the poor.

evidence.note: Absalom: every man with a dispute would come to me “וְהִצְדַּקְתִּיו”.
“Judge the poor and the orphan; the afflicted and destitute הַצְדִּיקוּ.”

senses.definition: To bring many to be righteous: the work of the righteous servant, who bears their iniquities, and of those who turn many to righteousness in the last days.

evidence.note: “בְּדַעְתּוֹ יַצְדִּיק צַדִּיק עַבְדִּי לָרַבִּים, and he will bear their iniquities.”
“וּמַצְדִּיקֵי הָרַבִּים like the stars forever and ever.”
“Through the obedience of the one the many will be made righteous (δίκαιοι κατασταθήσονται οἱ πολλοί).”

senses.definition: To make out one's own innocence.

evidence.note: Judah: “What shall we say … וּמַה נִּצְטַדָּק? God has found out the iniquity of your servants.”

evidence.locator: Psa.143.2, יִצְדַּק → δικαιωθήσεται; Psa.51.6, תִּצְדַּק → δικαιωθῇς; Isa.53.11, יַצְדִּיק → δικαιῶσαι; Gen.38.26 → δεδικαίωται; Gen.44.16 → δικαιωθῶμεν; δικαιόω renders צָדֵק ×12

evidence.note: Psa 143:2: “ἐξ ἔργων νόμου οὐ δικαιωθήσεται πᾶσα σὰρξ ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ”; also Gal 2:16.
Psa 51:6 quoted: “ὅπως ἂν δικαιωθῇς ἐν τοῖς λόγοις σου.”
“Believing on him who justifies the ungodly (τὸν δικαιοῦντα τὸν ἀσεβῆ).”
“Was not Abraham our father justified by works (ἐξ ἔργων ἐδικαιώθη) when he offered Isaac?”

opposites.note: “Condemn, declare guilty”: the other half of the judge's sentence.

words.summary: Once, in Daniel's counsel to Nebuchadnezzar. Its parallel, “showing mercy to the poor”, shows righteousness as right dealing with the needy, as the Hebrew צְדָקָה of Psa 112:9 and the Peshitta's זֵדְקְתָא “alms”.

senses.definition: Doing right, set beside showing mercy to the poor, by which the king is to break off his sins.

evidence.note: “וַחֲטָאָךְ בְּצִדְקָה פְרֻק וַעֲוָיָתָךְ בְּמִחַן עֲנָיִן”: break off your sins by righteousness and your iniquities by showing mercy to the poor.

words.gloss: be right, fitting; justify; be justified
words.summary: The Peshitta's verb of the root, spelled with ז (see the entry's note). The peal, impersonal, is “it is right, fitting”; the pael is “justify”; the ethpaal “be justified”, the word of Rom 3–5, Gal 2–3 and Jas 2.

senses.definition: What is due or must be: the Messiah's suffering, the high priest fitting for us, the wife's submission as is fitting.

evidence.note: “Thus it is written, and thus זָדֵֿק the Messiah to suffer and to rise” (Greek ἔδει).
“Such a high priest זָדֵֿק for us” (Greek ἔπρεπεν).
“Therefore it was right (זָדֵֿק) for him to be made like his brothers in all things” (Greek ὤφειλεν).
“As is fitting (דּזָדֵֿק) in the Lord” (Greek ἀνῆκεν).

senses.definition: God's act of justifying the one who believes; and men's justifying of themselves, or of God.

evidence.note: “Whom he called, these he also justified (זַדֵּק).”
“God is the one who justifies (מזַדֵּק).”
“Believing on him who justifies (דַּמזַדֵּק) the ungodly.”
“You are those who justify (דַּמזַדּקִינ) yourselves before men.”
The people and the tax collectors “justified (זַדֵּקו) God”.
The tax collector “went down to his house justified (מזַדַּק)”.

senses.definition: To be counted righteous by God: by faith and not by the works of the law (Paul); by works, which complete faith (James).

evidence.note: “Being justified (דֵּאזדַּדַּקנ) by faith, we have peace with God.”
“A man is not justified (מֵזדַּדַּק) by the works of the law, but by the faith of Jesus Christ.”
“Was not Abraham our father justified (אֵזדַּדַּק) by works when he offered Isaac?”
“By works a man is justified (מֵזדַּדַּק), and not by faith only.”
“By your words you will be justified (תֵּזדַּדַּק).”

senses.definition: Righteous before God, set against sinners and the wicked; and the title of Jesus, the Righteous One.

evidence.note: Zechariah and Elizabeth “were both righteous (זַדִּיקִינ) before God, walking in all the commandments”.
Hab 2:4: “the righteous (דּזַדִּיקָא) shall live by faith”.
The angels “will separate the wicked from among the righteous (זַדִּיקֵא)”.
“You denied the holy and righteous one (וזַדִּיקָא).”
“The righteous (זַדִּיקָא) for the unrighteous.”
“Jesus Christ the righteous (זַדִּיקָא).”

senses.definition: Righteousness reckoned to faith, the righteousness that is from God, and righteousness done.

evidence.note: Gen 15:6: “it was reckoned to him for righteousness” (לזַדִּיקֻו); also Gal 3:6; Jas 2:23.
“The blessedness of the man to whom God reckons righteousness (זַדִּיקֻותָֿא) without works.”
“Not having my own righteousness which is of the law, but … the righteousness which is from God by faith.”
“That we might become the righteousness (זַדִּיקֻותָֿא) of God in him.”
“Seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness (וזַדִּיקֻותֵֿה).”
“New heavens and a new earth in which righteousness dwells.”
“He who does righteousness is righteous.”

words.summary: The Peshitta's word for alms, where the Greek has ἐλεημοσύνη: righteousness shown in gifts to the poor, as Daniel's צִדְקָה beside “mercy to the poor” (Dan 4:24).

senses.definition: What is given to the poor, done before God and not to be seen by men.

evidence.note: “When you do alms (זֵדֿקתָֿא), do not sound a trumpet before you”; also Mat 6:1, 3–4.
Cornelius “did many alms (זֵדֿקָתָֿא) to the people”.
“Your prayers and your alms (וזֵדֿקָתָֿכֿ) have gone up for a memorial before God.”
The lame man laid at the gate “to ask alms”.
“Sell your possessions and give alms.”

words.summary: Once in the Peshitta New Testament (1Co 7:31), and its sense there is uncertain; it is kept as the Peshitta's word for what is proper, right.

senses.definition: What is proper or right; in 1Co 7:31 of using the world within what is proper.

evidence.note: “Those who use this world, as not abusing it”: the Peshitta's זֵדֿקָא stands where the Greek has καταχρώμενοι.

senses.definition: In a righteous way.

evidence.note: “Awake righteously (δικαίως; Peshitta זַדִּיקָאיִתֿ) and do not sin.”

cognates.gloss: speak the truth, be true; (II) hold true, believe; ṣidq truth, soundness
cognates.note: Arabic's verb is truthfulness, the agreement of what is said with the fact; its noun ṣidq is also soundness, firmness, and ṣadq is said of a spear that is hard and straight. This meets the Hebrew where צֶדֶק is right speech (Psa 52:5; Pro 12:17) and where צָדֵק is being in the right so that men say “Truth” (Isa 43:9).

evidence.note: “He spoke, said, uttered, or told, truth, or truly, or veraciously.”
II “He attributed … truth … to him … believed, what he said”; صَدْقٌ “Hard … or even, or straight” of a spear; صِدْقٌ “Truth; veracity … Hardness; firmness, compactness, or soundness”.

cognates.gloss: alms, a gift to the poor for God's sake
cognates.note: The same use as the Peshitta's זֵדְקְתָא and Daniel's צִדְקָה beside mercy to the poor. Possible only: the Arabic word may have been borrowed from Aramaic rather than formed in Arabic, which the dictionary does not settle.

evidence.note: “[An alms; i. e.] a gift … to the poor … for the sake of God.”

cognates.gloss: law, right, justness; justice, uprightness; justification; truth
cognates.note: Ge'ez keeps ጸ (ṣ) apart from ፀ (ṣ́), and the word is written with ጸ. The verb ṣadqa is “be just”.

evidence.note: “law, right, justness … justice; innocence, piety, probity, uprightness … imputed justice, justification … truth”.

evidence.locator: SEM000389 ṣdq [just] V, GEZ005461 ṣadqa [just] V

cognates.note: In the Kirta epic the king's wife is att ṣdqh, “the wife of his right”, his lawful wife: the rightful one, as Phoenician ṣmḥ ṣdq is the rightful heir and Hebrew צֶמַח צַדִּיק the righteous branch of David (Jer 23:5).

evidence.note: “att ṣdqh 1.14:I:12 ‘his legitimate wife’” (read from the OCR text, where it is garbled as “att.sdgh”; the PDF page was not rendered).

cognates.note: A king of Karatepe says every king made him a father “because of my righteousness (bṣdqy) and my wisdom”: righteousness as a ruler's virtue, as the Hebrew צְדָקָה of the king.

evidence.note: “[Heb. ṣedeq] n. 1. JUSTNESS, RIGHTEOUSNESS”, KAI 26 A I 12/13 b-ṣdqy wb-ḥkmty, “because of my righteousness and because of my intelligence”.
“[Heb. ṣ-d-q] v. yiph'il BE GOOD, RIGHTEOUS”, KAI 154.1/2 (Neo-Punic), “She was a good person.”

cognates.note: “A righteous king” in the Byblos inscriptions; and ṣmḥ ṣdq, “legitimate scion”, the rightful heir to the throne, the very words of Jer 23:5, צֶמַח צַדִּיק.

evidence.note: “[Heb. ṣaddiq] adj. 1. GOOD, RIGHTEOUS”, KAI 4.6 “for he is a righteous and honorable king”; KAI 10.8/9 “for he is a righteous king”; “2. LEGITIMATE, LEGAL”, KAI 43.11 l-ṣmḥ ṣdq “on behalf of the legitimate <royal> scion”, KAI 16 bn ṣdq “his legitimate successor”.
“[Heb. ṣemaḥ ṣaddiq, Je 23:5] n.ex. LEGITIMATE SON, HEIR APPARENT TO THE THRONE”.

evidence.locator: SEM000389 ṣdq [just] V, PUN001731 ṣdq [good] A

cognates.gloss: (verb) grant, fulfil an obligation; (noun) right, due; (adj.) proper, fitting; truth
cognates.note: Sabaic (Old South Arabian), which keeps ṣ apart from ṣ́ and ẓ. Its noun is a man's right or due, as צְדָקָה is in 2Sa 19:29 and Neh 2:20; its adjective is what is proper and fitting.

evidence.note: Verb “GRANT, FULFILL an obligation”, R3945/2 “the day when (the gods) … fulfilled their obligations”; noun ṣdq(m) “(1) RIGHT, DUE”, R3945/1–2 “doing (what was) right”, Gl 1574/10 “to restore to A. (his) due”, C86/12 bġyr ṣdqm “illegally”; “(2) adj: PROPER, APPROPRIATE”; ṣdqm “TRUTH, REALITY”.

cognates.gloss: be clear, just; (aphel) justify, do justice to
cognates.note: Jewish Aramaic, in the Targum of the same psalms: “be righteous” (Psa 19:10) and the aphel “do justice to” (Psa 82:3). Aramaic צ stands only for older ṣ.

evidence.note: “to be clear, just. Targ. Ps. XIX, 10 … Af. to justify, do justice to. Ib. LXXXII, 3.”

evidence.locator: SEM000389 ṣdq [just] V, ARM025315 ṢDQ [guiltless] V

evidence.note: Targ. Ps. XXXVII 21; V 13; XI 7; plural צַדִּיקִין Ib. I 5; XIV 5.

doctrine.statement: Yahweh brought Abram outside and said, “count the stars … so shall your seed be”; “and he believed (וְהֶאֱמִן) in Yahweh, and he counted it to him (וַיַּחְשְׁבֶהָ לּוֹ) as righteousness” (Gen 15:5–6). Paul quotes the verse and reasons from it: to one who works, the wage is reckoned as a debt; to one who does not work but believes on him who justifies the ungodly, his faith is reckoned as righteousness (Rom 4:3–5). He joins David's words with the same verb: “happy is the man to whom Yahweh does not reckon (לֹא יַחְשֹׁב) iniquity” (Psa 32:1–2), the man whose sin is covered and to whom God reckons righteousness without works (Rom 4:6–8). It was reckoned before Abraham was circumcised (Rom 4:10), and it was written not for him only but for us, to whom it will be reckoned who believe on him who raised Jesus our lord from the dead, who was delivered for our offences and raised for our justification (Rom 4:23–25). Those who are of faith are Abraham's sons, and if Christ's, Abraham's seed and heirs according to the promise (Gal 3:6–7, 29). The law itself says the same from the other side: Israel did not go in to possess the land for its own righteousness (Deu 9:4–6), and Daniel prays “not on our righteousnesses, but on your great compassions” (Dan 9:18). From the verses: God counts a man righteous because he believes God's promise, not because his works have earned it; and the promise believed is the promise to Abraham and his seed, which is Christ.

James quotes the same verse and says it was “fulfilled” when Abraham offered Isaac: “was not Abraham our father justified by works when he offered Isaac his son on the altar? You see that faith worked with his works, and by works faith was made complete; and the scripture was fulfilled which says, Abraham believed God, and it was reckoned to him as righteousness” (Jas 2:21–23). At the altar Yahweh swore “because you have done this thing … because you have listened to my voice” (Gen 22:16–18). James concludes that a man is justified by works and not by faith only, for faith without works is dead (Jas 2:17, 24, 26). The Hebrew word speaks the same way: צְדָקָה is what a man does, “to do righteousness and justice” (Gen 18:19); the righteous man of Ezekiel walks in Yahweh's statutes and lives, but if he turns from his righteousness all his righteous deeds are not remembered (Ezk 18:5–9, 24; 33:13); and Phinehas's zeal “was counted to him as righteousness” (Psa 106:31). Habakkuk says “the righteous will live by his faithfulness (בֶּאֱמוּנָתוֹ)” (Hab 2:4), quoted for faith in Rom 1:17, Gal 3:11 and Heb 10:38, where it goes on: “if he draws back, my soul has no pleasure in him; but we are not of those who draw back to destruction, but of faith to the saving of the soul” (Heb 10:38–39). From the verses: the faith reckoned for righteousness is a trust that obeys and continues; Paul and James describe one faith, Paul against works that would earn, James against a faith that does nothing.

The law forbids a judge to justify the wicked: the judges are to “justify the righteous and condemn the wicked” (Deu 25:1), Yahweh says “I will not justify the wicked” (Exo 23:7), and “he who justifies the wicked and he who condemns the righteous are both an abomination to Yahweh” (Pro 17:15). No man living is righteous before God (Psa 143:2; Ecc 7:20), and Paul draws from the psalm that by the works of the law no flesh will be justified (Rom 3:20; Gal 2:16). Yet Paul says God “justifies the ungodly” who believes (Rom 4:5), and he gives the reason: God set forth Christ Jesus as a ἱλαστήριον (the Greek word for the כַּפֹּרֶת, the cover of the ark, Exo 25:17; Heb 9:5) through faith in his blood, to show his righteousness, “that he might be righteous and the one who justifies him who is of the faith of Jesus” (Rom 3:24–26). Isaiah had said it of the servant: “by his knowledge my righteous servant will justify many (יַצְדִּיק … לָרַבִּים), and he will bear their iniquities” (Isa 53:11), and the servant himself says “he who justifies me is near” (Isa 50:8), words Paul takes up, “God is the one who justifies; who is he that condemns? Christ who died, and more, was raised” (Rom 8:33–34). Paul calls him “the one man Jesus Christ”, through whose obedience the many will be made righteous (Rom 5:15, 19). From the verses: God remains righteous in justifying sinners because sin was condemned and borne in the death of the righteous servant, a man raised by God, and the justified are those who share by faith in what was done in him.

Yahweh promises: “I will raise up to David a righteous branch (צֶמַח צַדִּיק), and he shall reign as king and act wisely, and do justice and righteousness in the land (בָּאָרֶץ). In his days Judah will be saved and Israel will dwell safely, and this is his name by which he will be called: יַהְוֶה צִדְקֵנוּ, Yahweh our righteousness” (Jer 23:5–6). In Jer 33:15–16 the promise is repeated and the same name is given to Jerusalem: “this is what one will call her: יַהְוֶה צִדְקֵנוּ”. The name is a sentence about Yahweh, borne by the king and by the city alike: it does not make either of them Yahweh, but says that their righteousness is Yahweh's. Paul says Christ “became to us wisdom from God, and righteousness and holiness and redemption” (1Co 1:30). The branch is David's son on David's throne (Isa 9:6; Jer 33:15), a king who reigns in righteousness (Isa 32:1) and judges the poor in righteousness and slays the wicked with the breath of his lips (Isa 11:4–5), and his rule is in the land. The psalms say Yahweh “will judge the world (תֵּבֵל) in righteousness” (Psa 9:9; 96:13; 98:9), and Paul says God has fixed a day in which he will judge the world in righteousness “by a man whom he has appointed, having given assurance to all by raising him from the dead” (Act 17:31). Peter looks for “new heavens and a new earth, in which righteousness dwells” (2Pe 3:13). From the verses: the righteousness promised to David's line is to be done on the earth, by a man of David's line whom God has raised from the dead, when he reigns as king over Judah and Israel and judges the world.

Gabriel tells Daniel: “seventy sevens are determined for your people and for your holy city, to finish transgression and to seal up sins, and to cover iniquity (וּלְכַפֵּר עָון), and to bring in everlasting righteousness (צֶדֶק עֹלָמִים), and to seal up vision and prophet, and to anoint a holy of holies” (Dan 9:24); after the sixty-two sevens “an anointed one (מָשִׁיחַ) will be cut off, and have nothing” (Dan 9:26). Hebrews says Christ appeared “once at the end of the ages to put away sin by the sacrifice of himself” (Heb 9:26), and Paul that “now, apart from the law, the righteousness of God has been made manifest”, shown in Christ set forth in his blood (Rom 3:21, 25–26). From the verses: the everlasting righteousness of Daniel's prophecy is brought in by the anointed one who is cut off, whose death covers iniquity.

Ezekiel sets the righteous and the wicked side by side: the soul that sins, it will die; the righteousness of the righteous will be upon him; the righteous man, “living he will live” (Ezk 18:9, 20–22). Proverbs says “righteousness delivers from death” (Pro 10:2; 11:4) and “in the path of righteousness is life, and in its pathway no death” (Pro 12:28). Yet the righteous die like other men: “the righteous perishes, and no man lays it to heart” (Isa 57:1); “there is a righteous man who perishes in his righteousness” (Ecc 7:15); one event comes to the righteous and to the wicked (Ecc 9:2). The life is therefore not exemption from dying but life after it: David says “I, in righteousness, will see your face; I will be satisfied when I awake (בְהָקִיץ) with your likeness” (Psa 17:15), and Daniel that many who sleep in the dust of the earth will awake (יָקִיצוּ), some to everlasting life and some to shame, and “those who make many righteous (מַצְדִּיקֵי הָרַבִּים)” will shine like the stars forever (Dan 12:2–3). From the verses: the righteous, like all men, die and sleep in the dust; their life is the life of the resurrection, when they awake.

note: Drafted 2026-11-18. Root key צדק, as the corpus and BDB key it; no other entry had it. BDB keys: r.ar.ae צַדִּיק, r.ar.ac צְדָקָה, r.ar.ab צֶדֶק, r.ar.ad צָדֵק, and xr.ac.ae Aramaic צִדְקָה (Dan 4:24). r.ar.aa is the bare root heading and is not assigned. The brief counts צֶדֶק by spelling, so r.ar.ab also takes the names מַלְכִּי־צֶדֶק (Gen 14:18; Psa 110:4) and אֲדֹנִי־צֶדֶק (Jos 10:1, 3), and other names' keys (a.be.ag, m.cd.aq) count צֶדֶק's tokens. Names: Zadok r.ar.af, Zedekiah r.ar.ag, Jehozadak/Jozadak e.az.av and Aramaic xj.ad.ae, Melchizedek m.cd.aq, each in names/; Adoni-zedek already has names/adoni-zedek.json under אדנ (adon), whose note says no צדק entry existed to link to: it can now. Stems: the brief lists Ezk 16:52 under both the qal (תִּצְדַּקְנָה) and the piel (בְּצַדֶּקְתֵּךְ); both are cited, under piel only. The Peshitta spells the root זדק (SEDRA root זדק; lexemes 845 זדיקא, 846 זדיקאית, 847 זדיקותא, 848 זדק, 850 זדקא, 851 זדקתא), with ז for the expected צ before ד; the brief's Peshitta section found nothing because it looked for צדק. Syriac lemmas are pointed from SEDRA's vocalised forms in the database, normalised (ֻו written וּ, rafe dropped). Peshitta form numbers: 1 peal (זָדֵק “it is right”), 3 pael, 4 ethpaal. זֵדְקָא (1Co 7:31) is uncertain; its sense is taken from SEDRA's gloss “propriety”. Greek: the brief offers δίκαιος as a loan from צַדִּיק on Thayer's “prop. the Hebr. צַדִּיק”; that is a remark on meaning, not an etymology, and δίκαιος is a native Greek word from δίκη, so it is recorded only as a rendering. Ugaritic: Segert's ṣdqh (p. 115) is read from OCR (“sdgh”); check the PDF, and DULAT s.v. ṣdq (not consulted) for the noun “legitimacy, rightness” and the personal name ṣdqn (KTU 4.286:2, Segert glossary p. 198). Ugaritic ṣ does not tell ṣ from ṣ́, so no sounds are recorded for it. Leads not followed: Dillmann's Lexicon col. for ጸደቀ (not local); CAL for Old and Imperial Aramaic ṣdq and ṣdqh (Nerab, Panamuwa); Payne Smith for ܙܕܩ; Akkadian has no ṣdq root (Oracc none). The Arabic صَدَقَة “alms” is recorded as possible because it may be a loan from Aramaic; if it is native Arabic it is a cognate of זֵדְקְתָא and Dan 4:24. Doctrine to review: all six statements are reasoned conclusions from the cited verses; ‘righteous-branch-and-kingdom’ reads Jer 33:16's naming of Jerusalem as showing that יַהְוֶה צִדְקֵנוּ is a sentence about Yahweh, not an identification; ‘everlasting-righteousness’ joins Dan 9:24 to Heb 9:26 and Rom 3:21–26.
